text: RESULTS: EMG and Nerve Conduction Studies reveal bilateral lower motor neuron signs consistent with anterior horn cell involvement, showing reduced recruitment and fibrillation potentials in the upper extremities. Combined with the MRI findings of a syrinx extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region, these results are diagnostic of Syringomyelia (likely secondary to a Chiari malformation given the clinical context). The clinical picture of pain out of proportion to exam findings, followed by weakness, fasciculations, and a "cape-like" distribution of sensory loss (temperature and pain absent over chest and arms) with preserved vibration and proprioception is classic for this condition.
